consensus_findings.description: Critical: The rate-limit endpoint specifies authentication but not authorization or trustworthy attribution. Any valid coordinator key can target any known lane and self-assert `source` and `observed_at`. Existing coordination_api.py already provides bound principals, anti-spoof identity resolution, and operation authorization, but the plan does not require their use and OpenAPI defines no 403 response.

Critical: Legacy roadmap outcomes use a third identity namespace (`vendor_limit:claude`) that is neither `AgentEntry.name` (`claude-local`) nor `AgentEntry.type` (`claude_code`). The plan correctly rejects provider-only observations that match multiple lanes, but never specifies how dispatch context resolves short names like `claude` into an unambiguous lane `agent_id` before POST `/vendors/{agent_id}/rate-limit-observations`, nor what happens when only the short name is available (404 vs bounded skip vs fail-closed reporting).

Nit: The current result grammar can report vendor_limit:claude without the concrete AgentEntry lane, while the plan correctly rejects ambiguous provider-only writes; the plan must define how dispatch context supplies agent_id before implementation.

Legacy dispatch outcomes emit provider-level names ('vendor_limit:claude:...'), whereas Design D2 and OpenAPI POST /vendors/{agent_id}/rate-limit-observations require exact lane IDs ('agent_id', e.g., 'claude-local'). Design D2 mandates rejecting provider-only observations that match multiple lanes. Without preserving the executed lane ID in dispatch results, rate-limit observations targeting multi-lane provider types like 'claude' will be rejected or return 404 Not Found.

policy.py requires a scalar cost delta between vendors, whereas dg-00 CatalogService returns multi-model input/output token pricing objects (CostProjection.models). In agents.yaml, primary agents specify model: null, leaving model resolution to runtime archetypes. The spec and design fail to define a deterministic conversion formula (model selection rule and input/output token weightings) to derive scalar vendor pricing from catalog model arrays.

work-packages.yaml omits skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py and skills/autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py from all write_allow scopes. Tasks 3.5 and 3.6 require dispatcher-observed rate-limit reporting, but work-package scopes prevent workers from adding rate-limit observation calls to these dispatchers.

The lane-to-catalog matching key is undefined, so 'catalog-derived cost projections for every configured dispatch lane' cannot be met. model_catalog rows are keyed (vendor, model, endpoint_kind) where vendor is the OpenRouter slug ('anthropic', 'openai') or 'local'; AgentEntry carries type='claude_code', cli.model=null for claude-local (resolved later via archetypes.yaml), and sdk.model='claude-sonnet-4-6' with endpoint_kind unset. No existing mapping joins vendor_type to catalog vendor, so every CLI lane would project cost=unknown and the 'Catalog pricing is available' policy scenario can never fire in production.

Watchdog probe persistence (tasks 3.1/3.2, 'Watchdog records a probe') will never run in the deployed coordinator. WatchdogService._check_vendor_health loads skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/vendor_health.py by filesystem path and silently returns when it is absent; the production Dockerfile copies only skills/shared/github_classifier.py, so the file does not exist in the container and every lane stays 'unknown' (and is excluded from available_only reads).

No work package can edit the code that actually observes rate limits, so task 3.6 'Ingest dispatcher-observed limits' has no caller. vendor_limit_reporter.py is a new file in wp-bridge-policy, but provider_dispatch.py (skills/autopilot/scripts, provider strings 'claude_code'/'codex'), review_dispatcher.py (_CAPACITY_PATTERNS, SdkRateLimitError), and the autopilot-roadmap SKILL.md prompt layer that emits 'vendor_limit:<vendor>:<reason>' are all outside every write_allow. The only in-scope caller is orchestrator.py, which sees a free-text vendor token, not a lane.

Three vendor namespaces collide and the plan defines no translation: roadmap policy and _STATIC_COST_TIERS use 'claude'/'codex'/'pi'; provider_dispatch and AgentEntry.type use 'claude_code'; lane IDs are 'claude-local'/'claude-remote'. D7 says alternates are 'grouped by vendor type' (claude_code) but Policy.preferred_vendor and VendorLimit.vendor arrive as 'claude', so preferred_vendor matching, the limited-lane exclusion, and static-tier fallback all silently miss. The legacy 'vendor_limit:claude' outcome therefore cannot become an unambiguous lane observation without a documented resolution rule.

'Registry is unavailable → bounded injected fallback provider or fail closed' regresses the common local runtime. autopilot-roadmap runs with the host LLM as runtime and frequently no coordinator (this session reports Transport: none); today _handle_vendor_limit always has five alternates, so a rate limit yields a switch. After removal of the roster, an unreachable coordinator with no injected provider turns every vendor limit into fail_closed, halting roadmap execution.

A rate-limit observation with reset_at NULL (allowed by the contract and by RateLimitObservation, where both reset_at and retry_after_seconds are optional) is 'active' forever under D4, so one unbounded observation permanently excludes a lane until an operator deletes the row. This contradicts the proposal's 'expired limits stop excluding lanes without operator repair'.

Critical: Legacy `vendor_limit:claude:<reason>` outcomes cannot produce the lane-scoped observations required by design.md:10-15. The existing outcome carries only `claude`, while agents.yaml defines both `claude-local` and `claude-remote` with provider type `claude_code`; provider_dispatch.py also carries provider/model but no lane ID. The outcome is therefore unmatched or ambiguous and cannot safely persist a limit.

Critical: The policy boundary loses lane identity. design.md:46-49 removes one limited lane and then groups remaining lanes by provider type, but policy.py accepts flat vendor strings, compares them directly with `VendorLimit.vendor`, and returns only a provider string. The plan does not define how `from_vendor`, preferred vendors, cost lookups, decision records, and the next dispatch preserve both `lane_id` and `vendor_type`.

Critical: The static pricing fallback in design.md:48-49 and tasks.md:35 contradicts the catalog-only behavior in proposal.md:14-15 and spec.md:21-25. policy.py's `_STATIC_COST_TIERS` is a second in-code price table whose normalized values can populate `expected_cost_delta_usd` and enforce a USD ceiling even when the catalog projection is required to be unknown.

Critical: No deterministic join is defined from a lane to dg-00 catalog rows. CatalogService keys rows by `(vendor, model, endpoint_kind)`, while AgentEntry exposes a lane type and optional CLI/SDK/endpoint fields, many configured CLI models are null, and OpenRouter catalog vendors such as `anthropic` do not equal lane types such as `claude_code`. Independent implementations can select different rows or return unknown for the same lane.

Critical: Per-model catalog prices cannot deterministically become the scalar policy delta compared with `cost_ceiling_usd`. spec.md:101-105 mentions model and token assumptions, but the plan defines no model-selection rule, prompt/completion token quantities, formula, stale-price rule, tie-break, units, or rounding. OpenAPI's `CostProjection.models` items are unconstrained objects, whereas dg-00 stores separate prompt and completion USD-per-million-token prices.

Critical: Local endpoint availability is left in dg-00's catalog by design.md:5-8, but the effective availability precedence in design.md:25-30 and spec.md:48-51 considers only lane limits and watchdog probe snapshots. A local lane can therefore appear available or dispatchable while CatalogService's local probe marks its endpoint/model unavailable or stale. The plan must define how catalog-local health gates lane availability without duplicating its state.

Critical: Probe freshness is optional end-to-end. design.md:25-30 requires stale evidence to become unknown, but contracts/db/schema.sql makes `stale_after` nullable, the event schema also permits null, and neither the spec nor tasks define a TTL source, default, or exact expiry boundary. A first successful or failed probe can remain authoritative forever after watchdog failure or restart.

Critical: Rate-limit expiry is nondeterministic. OpenAPI permits `reset_at` and `retry_after_seconds` to be both absent or both present, storage retains only nullable `reset_at`, and no precedence, maximum horizon, server-time conversion, supersession, or null-reset behavior is specified. A valid observation can exclude a lane indefinitely or be normalized differently by different callers.

Critical: Registry-unavailable behavior is left as two materially different choices—use a bounded injected fallback provider or fail closed—in spec.md:107-111. The plan does not define the default, what bounds the fallback, its freshness or provenance, capability filtering, or behavior for timeout, 401/403, 404, 5xx, and malformed responses. An implementation can silently recreate the forbidden hardcoded roster.

Critical: Tasks 3.5-3.6 require dispatcher-result metadata and ingestion, but wp-bridge-policy owns no existing dispatcher result producer. Its write scope omits `skills/autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py` and `skills/autopilot/scripts/tests/test_provider_dispatch.py`; the current normalizer drops metadata beyond outcome, handoff, model, and warnings. A new reporter with no scoped caller cannot supply canonical lane/reset data.

Critical: The verification plan cannot prove tasks 5.1-5.2. wp-integration's sole verification command is strict OpenSpec validation, despite tasks requiring focused suites, regressions, Ruff, mypy, and work-package gates. wp-api-producers also omits the existing `test_watchdog_vendor.py` compatibility suite and does not execute the vendor_health test it permits modifying.

Critical: The plan does not require registry persistence failures to be isolated from existing WatchdogService transition events. watchdog.py currently wraps probing, first-run baseline logic, persistence insertion points, and `vendor.unavailable`/`vendor.recovered` emission in one broad exception boundary. A failed snapshot write could suppress legacy events, yet tasks.md:25-26 has no persistence-failure scenario.

Critical: D7/spec say roadmap alternates are capability-filtered lanes grouped by `vendor_type`, but `policy.py` / `orchestrator.py` today key `available_vendors`, `preferred_vendor`, and `_STATIC_COST_TIERS` on short names (`claude`, `codex`, …). The plan does not define the collapse rule from lane records → the `list[str]` policy consumes (one lane per type? type strings? short names?), so removing the hardcoded roster will break preferred-vendor matching and static fallback pricing.

Critical: Catalog-only pricing is required, and the catalog-pricing scenario mentions model and token assumptions, but neither design nor contracts define (a) how a lane joins `model_catalog` rows (`AgentEntry.type` vs OpenRouter `vendor` prefixes like `anthropic` vs lane model ids), or (b) the deterministic formula that turns `prompt_usd_per_mtok`/`completion_usd_per_mtok` into the scalar `Callable[[str], float | None]` policy already expects.

Critical: Tasks 3.5–3.6 require dispatcher-result rate-limit reset metadata and ingestion, but work-package write scopes only add a new `vendor_limit_reporter.py` and omit the live producers that already classify capacity (`skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`, which has both `agent_id` and capacity errors) and `skills/autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. The current `vendor_limit:<vendor>:<reason>` grammar also cannot carry `reset_at`/`retry_after`.

Nit: Probe rows expose nullable `stale_after` and D4 treats stale evidence as `unknown`, but no requirement sets the default probe TTL, who writes `stale_after`, or how it relates to `VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. Implementers can leave probes forever-fresh or immediately stale.

Nit: OpenAPI accepts both `reset_at` and `retry_after_seconds`, and design calls them optional, but there is no rule for converting retry-after into an absolute reset, precedence when both are present, or whether a limit with neither field remains active forever. Spec expiry only covers “when a stored reset time is reached.”
Nit: The plan exposes raw per-model catalog prices but does not yet specify the deterministic model and token assumptions used to produce the scalar policy cost delta.

wp-bridge-policy in work-packages.yaml specifies depends_on: [wp-registry-core] but omits wp-api-producers. wp-bridge-policy implements HTTP bridge helpers in coordination_bridge.py that call GET /vendors and POST /vendors/{agent_id}/rate-limit-observations. Omitting wp-api-producers from depends_on allows parallel execution of bridge code before the HTTP endpoints in coordination_api.py are implemented.

WatchdogService._check_vendor_health() currently skips persistence on its first run to establish a baseline without emitting false transition events. Task 3.1 requires persisting probe snapshots on the first run, but the plan does not specify how initial baseline rows are written to vendor_probe_state without triggering false vendor.unavailable pg_notify events for offline vendors on coordinator startup.

Task 4.4 removes the hardcoded vendor list from orchestrator.py, and spec.md requires using an injected fallback provider or failing closed when the coordinator is unavailable. However, the plan lacks a concrete interface definition or parameter contract for how RoadmapOrchestrator receives and handles the fallback provider when COORDINATION_API_URL is unreachable.

Staleness is asserted but never defined. D4 says 'missing or stale evidence is unknown' and the probe table has stale_after, yet nothing states who sets stale_after or its relationship to VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 5 min). The spec requirement 'Live Availability State' omits the stale-to-unknown transition entirely, so it is untested by the spec.

Lanes without a CLI section never get a probe. check_all_vendors skips agents without 'cli', and load_agents_yaml's HTTP path uses /agents/dispatch-configs which drops non-dispatchable entries, so SDK-only or routable-endpoint lanes (and ocr-local) stay 'unknown' forever and are excluded from available_only=true reads. dg-00 local probes already cover endpoint_kind='local' rows in the catalog, but D1 gives no rule for merging that signal into lane status.

Any valid API key can mark any lane limited for up to 7 days (retry_after_seconds max 604800) with an unbounded metadata object and a caller-chosen 'source'. Keys are registry-derived per agent with trust levels, but the plan does not bind the observation to the principal or gate by trust, so a trust-level-1 key can blackhole routing for every other agent.

The OpenAPI contract declares BearerAuth only, but the bridge client (_http_request) sends X-API-Key and the coordinator's verify_api_key accepts Bearer, X-Coordinator-API-Key, and X-API-Key. Contract-parity tests written against v1.yaml will not describe how wp-bridge-policy actually authenticates, and D5's route naming ({lane_id}) differs from the contract and lock keys ({agent_id}).

retry_after_seconds has no anchor: the contract does not say whether reset_at = observed_at + retry_after (client clock, may be skewed or stale) or server receipt time + retry_after, nor which wins when both reset_at and retry_after_seconds are present. Also, replaying observation_id with a different agent_id is specified as 'idempotent' rather than a 409 conflict.

D7's 'request-scoped price projection' has no deterministic reduction to the scalar policy.py needs. _estimate_cost_delta_with_source takes a vendor→float lookup; the registry returns per-model prompt/completion USD-per-Mtok lists. Which model per provider, which token assumptions, and how prompt vs completion combine are unspecified, so the resulting cost_ceiling decisions are not reproducible across runs.

wp-api-producers edits skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/vendor_health.py and its tests but its verification step runs only coordinator pytest, so a vendor_health regression passes the gate. wp-integration is tier A yet its only verification is 'openspec validate --strict', with no test or lint command, so the merged tree is never exercised by the package that claims full validation.

Nit: The event and persistence contracts admit incompatible states. Probe events may use `status: limited`, although `vendor_probe_state.status` rejects it, and both event and POST schemas allow `scope: model` without a model value. Kind-discriminated status rules and a required non-empty model for model scope are needed.

Nit: design.md:39-42 calls `{available, result|error}` the repository bridge envelope, but coordination_bridge.py uses `status=ok|error|skipped`, `COORDINATOR_AVAILABLE`, transport, response/data, and error fields. A one-off registry envelope would make existing normalization and caller error handling inconsistent.

Nit: No requirement defines structured audit, logs, or metrics for accepted, duplicate, rejected, expired, or stale observations; catalog-match failures; persistence failures; or registry fallback activation. Operators would be unable to explain why a lane was excluded or why policy used degraded behavior without reconstructing database state.

Nit: Rate-limit observations have no retention or compaction policy, while `Availability.rate_limits` is an unpaginated array of unconstrained objects with no active-versus-history semantics. Unlimited unique observation IDs, especially those without resets, cause unbounded storage and response work despite the table being described as active runtime state.

Nit: The plan overloads `vendor` across lane IDs, legacy aliases, AgentEntry provider types, catalog vendors, and policy variables while alternately naming the same API identifier `id`, `lane_id`, and `agent_id`. Add a canonical vocabulary and typed mappings so future implementers can distinguish lane identity, provider grouping, catalog vendor, and legacy aliases.

Nit: Vendor Registry OpenAPI documents only `BearerAuth`, while `coordination_bridge._http_request` sends `X-API-Key` and the coordinator already accepts Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`. As written, a Bearer-only implementation would fail closed for the planned bridge writers despite D6 claiming API-key auth.

Nit: Design D6 requires bridge helpers to return the repository `{available, result|error}` envelope, but current coordination-bridge operations normalize to `{status, operation, COORDINATOR_AVAILABLE, reason|error|...}` skip/success shapes. Introducing a second envelope for `/vendors` will fork caller conventions.

Nit: `wp-bridge-policy` write_allow/verification target `skills/tests/coordination-bridge/**`, but the established `test_coordination_bridge.py` suite lives under `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/tests/` (not writable/verified). `wp-api-producers` also writes `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/vendor_health.py` and its tests yet verification runs only coordinator pytest, so producer regressions can merge green.

Nit: Spec scenario “Registry is unavailable” allows the orchestrator to use a bounded injected fallback provider or fail closed, without criteria for choosing either path. That underspecifies coordinator-unavailable behavior for the primary consumer of availability.

Nit: The plan preserves `vendor.unavailable` / `vendor.recovered` transitions but does not require structured logs/metrics for probe persistence failures, rejected ambiguous observations, auth failures on observation writes, or read-time expiry/staleness transitions—leaving the new failure modes hard to detect in production.

FYI: Watchdog today early-returns on the first health pass after seeding `_previous_vendor_state`, emitting no events and persisting nothing. Tasks 3.1–3.2 require first-and-later probe persistence while preserving transition-only events; implementers must persist before that return or first-boot availability stays `unknown` until the second interval.

contracts/openapi/v1.yaml Availability schema does not include stale_after, whereas db/schema.sql (vendor_probe_state) and contracts/events/vendor-availability.schema.json include stale_after. Additionally, the plan does not specify the default TTL duration used by WatchdogService when populating stale_after for probe snapshots.

Rate-limit ingestion emits nothing: the lock key names an event 'vendor.availabilityobserved' but no design decision emits it, no audit_log entry is written for POST observations, and expiry of a limit is silent. Operators cannot tell why a lane vanished from available_only reads or who reported it.

GET /vendors naturally becomes per-lane catalog and rate-limit queries (CatalogService only exposes list_entries/get_entry), and vendor_rate_limits rows are never purged, so the (agent_id, reset_at) index scans grow without bound.

Optional: Design D5 names the path parameter `lane_id` while OpenAPI, DB PK, event schema, and work-package lock keys all use `agent_id`. The dual vocabulary is accurate conceptually but invites mismatched client code.

Optional: `GET /vendors` has no pagination while projecting catalog costs per configured lane. Current roster size is small, so this is acceptable, but the contract should acknowledge the bound or add a soft cap if agent counts grow.

Lane identity correctly uses `AgentEntry.name` with `AgentEntry.type` as `vendor_type`, matching `/agents/dispatch-configs` (`agent_id`/`type`), `vendor_health.agent_id`/`vendor_type`, and watchdog transition `entity_id` keys; provider grouping is explicit rather than collapsing local/remote lanes.

TDD ordering is coherent across design D8, tasks (failing tests before implementation in sections 1–4), and work packages; additive SQL deliberately omits price columns so dg-00 remains the sole pricing store.

Parallel packages `wp-api-producers` and `wp-bridge-policy` both depend only on `wp-registry-core` and use disjoint write scopes (coordinator API/watchdog/vendor_health versus bridge/reporter/orchestrator/policy), so they do not collide on files when run concurrently.

Bridge coordinator-unavailable and unauthorized observation-write scenarios are specified as explicit unavailability / fail-closed rejection rather than empty successful registries, which matches existing bridge degrade-to-skipped behavior for other capabilities.
